pairs.question: Num Cicero?
pairs.derivation: Clean direct-speech confirm-question and its answer within a single line: "Num Cicero?" "Cicero". Question refers back to who coined the boopis nickname (istud qui nomen de more boopis fecit). Quoted exactly; only terminal punctuation normalized. The following "Qui? quaeso. Nonne patronus optimus ... ?" is a separate exchange (and its question carries an interior lacuna ...), so it is excluded.

pairs.question: Ten sanum, iucunde, rear?
pairs.answer: Si scribere versus insani est, dicas ambo insanire licebit.
pairs.derivation: Catullus asks whether he should think Calvus sane (Ten sanum, iucunde, rear?); the reply genuinely answers with a conditional retort. Answer taken as the single full sentence of the reply (line 70-71), ending at the full stop; what follows (Arreptoque stilo coepit perarare tabellas) is third-person narration, excluded. No inline verse number (70) intruded into the quoted span.

pairs.question: Cur, quaeso, iuvenis iubet me valere, Priape, cuius in tenero fides tanta amore reperta est? cui nemo facinus volens exprobraverit, unum praeter hoc miserae mihi, nolit ipse quod unus? Qui tamen sequitur malam stultus omnivolamque feminam, et magis et magis tanto deperit illam quanto digna minus minusque et videtur et ipsa est.
pairs.answer: In hortulo falce qui tibi tutus est mea, aspice ut mala dulcia pendent, aspice ut tibi et inminent sorba livida eidem.
pairs.derivation: The puella's entire speech to Priapus is one extended question/plea (Cur ... iubet me valere ...?), quoted verbatim and contiguous; the speech tag "Tristis adloquitur senem mox puella Priapum:" and the inline verse markers 115, 120 are stripped. Priapus's reply (introduced by the narration tag "Cui Priapus:", dropped) begins the answer; the answer window is his first sentence (to the first full stop) directing her to look at his garden's fruit. The remainder (Quae si sponte cadunt ... putidiora, with markers 125) elaborates the metaphor and is cut.

pairs.question: Te clausum gleba Pariorum marmoris una in lapicidinis delituisse ferunt aevi qui cursum, qui longa silentia labi audieris longis pervigil auriculis; cum vero cunei diviso marmore glebam solverunt, exstas protinus e lapide: dic age, quae tantum diducat labra voluptas et quo sis nobis nomine rite deus.
pairs.answer: Nullus eram latuique diu Silenus, et idem hic Genius bruti marmoris usque fui.
pairs.derivation: The interlocutor's whole speech is an address culminating in a double question (dic age, quae ... voluptas et quo sis ... nomine ... deus), quoted verbatim and contiguous; inline verse markers 130, 135 stripped, and the conversion artifact 'È' (a corrupted closing quote on deusE) removed so the word is plain 'deus'. Silenus's reply answers the name question in its first sentence: Nullus eram ... Silenus ... fui. (the artifact 'È' on eratE later in the reply is outside the quoted answer). The rest (Nil circum nisi marmor ...) digresses on the quarry and is cut.
